mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points signals weakening consumer demand, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE rises > 0.3pp (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) exceeding 2% signals deteriorating demand, which depresses corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when GDPC1 declines > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for 3 months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in unemployment rate and decline in nonfarm payrolls (UNRATE up and PAYEMS down) signals a deepening labor market downturn, which reduces earnings power and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE rises and PAYEMS falls (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) exceeding 1% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when INDPRO declines > 1% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 2-month increase in the housing starts index (HOUST) above 5% signals a strengthening housing market, which boosts consumer confidence and spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when HOUST rises > 5% (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 6-month increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above 2% signals a strengthening demand environment, which raises earnings expectations and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when GDPC1 rises > 2% (t-test p > 0.05).
